finding: Stochastic edits on a phylogeny jointly support reconstruction and phonological-change inference.
formalization_use: Use a probabilistic generator outside the proof kernel, with explicit tree and edit parameters.
caution: An inferred high-probability form is conditional on the model and cognate inputs.

finding: Markedness and cross-language features improve earlier probabilistic reconstruction on several families.
formalization_use: Separate well-formedness priors from evidence for historical correspondence.
caution: Known cognate groups and phylogenies are supplied; borrowing and reduplication remain outside this model.

finding: A generative phylogenetic model induces cognate groups and approximates weighted automata during inference.
formalization_use: Keep approximation error separate from correctness of a checked candidate.
caution: Approximated search is not a completeness certificate.

finding: Scalable cognate recovery trades cluster purity against recall on large Oceanic wordlists.
formalization_use: Report both false merges and missed cognates; retain intermediate clusters.
caution: High purity alone can hide excessive splitting.

finding: Pair HMMs learn word-pair similarities from training examples.
formalization_use: Implement an alignment baseline and a verifiable alignment witness.
caution: Surface similarity is evidence, not a definition of historical cognacy.

finding: Bayesian scoring joins proposed cognates and regular correspondences; an implementation tests Polish and Russian.
formalization_use: Make latent cognacy and correspondence parameters explicit.
caution: The study's small model and pairwise evaluation do not settle family-wide reconstruction.

finding: Etymological alignments are evaluated through probabilistic description of internal consistency.
formalization_use: Distinguish a reproducible objective function from historical validity.
caution: Absence of hand-coded vowel preferences does not make an algorithm assumption-free.

finding: Context and phonetic features improve etymological alignment and imputation.
formalization_use: Give rule contexts and feature encodings explicit semantics.
caution: Better imputation is not proof that a supplied etymological database is correct.

finding: LexStat learns language-specific scoring schemes for multilingual cognate detection.
formalization_use: Use a pinned LexStat implementation as a candidate generator and baseline.
caution: Do not promote heuristic clusters to premises without provenance and review.

finding: LingPy organizes comparison, alignment, cognacy and evaluation workflows.
formalization_use: Interoperate through exported data and certificates rather than reimplementing the whole toolkit in Lean.
caution: Tool execution and algorithmic correctness are distinct validation layers.

finding: Orthographic features help discriminate Romance cognates from borrowings.
formalization_use: Preserve distinct inherited and borrowed relation types.
caution: Writing conventions and the tested language pairs limit transfer to prehistoric data.

finding: Similarity networks identify partially cognate morphemes in Sino-Tibetan data.
formalization_use: Represent cognacy on morpheme occurrences, not only whole words.
caution: A compound can share one inherited component without sharing an entire lexical ancestor.

finding: SVMs combine alignment-based cognacy features across typologically diverse wordlists.
formalization_use: Include a strong non-neural cognacy baseline.
caution: Supervised generalization requires a split that prevents cognate-family leakage.

finding: EDICTOR supports manual segmentation, alignment, cognacy and correspondence inspection.
formalization_use: Use an expert-facing editor around a small verified core.
caution: An editable judgment needs versioned provenance; the interface does not certify it.

finding: Global rescoring and reranking improve cognate-detection score matrices.
formalization_use: Express global consistency constraints separately from pair scores.
caution: The operational NLP notion of cognate must be reconciled with strict historical inheritance.

finding: Dictionary-based cognate discovery combines sound correspondences with semantic representations.
formalization_use: Retain gloss evidence and semantic candidates alongside phonological evidence.
caution: Semantic embeddings propose comparisons; they cannot establish inherited meaning.

finding: Trees inferred from automatic cognates approach but generally lag expert-annotated inputs.
formalization_use: Evaluate cognate detection and phylogeny separately.
caution: Expert gold standards can also contain errors and must remain revisable.

finding: Compatible alignment sites form a graph; correspondence inference becomes a clique-cover problem.
formalization_use: Verify proposed pattern groups and preserve missing-data alternatives. The prototype proves compatibility need not be transitive.
caution: Compatibility requires shared non-gap evidence and no conflicts; connected components are not valid substitutes for cliques.

finding: A broad related-word pipeline covers cognate detection, borrowing discrimination and word production.
formalization_use: Separate relation classification from generated-word verification.
caution: Orthographic production is not the same task as phonological reconstruction.

finding: BipSkip and MAPLE provide fast cognate and tree inference for exploration.
formalization_use: Treat speed-oriented inference as an interchangeable front end.
caution: A MAP tree is a model-dependent estimate, not a proved genealogy.

finding: A stochastic splitting-and-merging model connects markedness with frequency distributions.
formalization_use: Provide explicit merger examples and optional probabilistic priors.
caution: Inventory-level frequency patterns do not uniquely identify lexical histories.

finding: Gaussian processes model covariance between Indo-Aryan sound-change outcomes.
formalization_use: Test independence assumptions instead of silently multiplying scores.
caution: Posterior predictive adequacy is an empirical property outside the kernel proof.

finding: An EM framework jointly estimates cognacy and sound-correspondence parameters.
formalization_use: Separate latent variables, observations and update algorithms.
caution: Convergence of a fitting procedure would not establish correctness of its linguistic model.

finding: DiaSim runs ordered sound-change cascades and diagnoses Latin-to-French errors.
formalization_use: Prioritize traceable forward derivation and useful mismatch reports.
caution: A cascade tuned on observed reflexes needs fresh held-out evaluation.

finding: Statistical and neural correspondence learners behave differently with data size, ambiguity and direction.
formalization_use: Benchmark forward and inverse tasks separately on synthetic and real data.
caution: Perfect artificial rules remove several difficulties present in historical evidence.

finding: Supervised neural reconstruction uses a large Romance dataset and analyzes phonological error types.
formalization_use: Use withheld attested ancestors as one evaluation track.
caution: The authors distinguish this supervised task from the harder work of historical reconstruction.

finding: South Asian historical data are often scattered rather than wholly absent.
formalization_use: Budget for source reconciliation and language-variety identifiers.
caution: Digitization does not automatically yield comparable transcriptions or licenses.

finding: Character-distribution change can detect some sound changes through historical spelling.
formalization_use: Model spelling as an observation channel over phonology.
caution: Orthographic change and sound change must not be equated.

finding: A shared task evaluates missing cognate reflex prediction across standardized families.
formalization_use: Reuse transparent splits, baselines and exact task definitions.
caution: Predicting a missing daughter word differs from reconstructing an unattested ancestor.

finding: Bayesian phylogenetic ancestral-state methods are adapted to cognate reflex prediction.
formalization_use: Make all intermediate cognacy, tree and alignment decisions inspectable.
caution: Uncertainty compounds across pipeline stages.

finding: Transformer and convolutional inpainting models predict missing reflexes from cognate sets.
formalization_use: Compare architecture choices without changing the evaluation target.
caution: Matrix position and missing-data conventions can encode unintended information.

finding: A transformer does not consistently outperform the rule-based shared-task baseline.
formalization_use: Require simple baselines before adding complex inference machinery.
caution: Small sparse datasets can favor simpler methods.

finding: Neural unsupervised reconstruction retains monotonic alignment and controlled underfitting biases.
formalization_use: Record alignment monotonicity as an assumption in the model configuration.
caution: A monotonic alignment model needs an explicit treatment of metathesis.

finding: Transformer reconstruction is tested on Romance and Chinese comparative datasets.
formalization_use: Use neural predictions as candidate sets, with language-family-specific evaluation.
caution: Performance against published labels does not make those labels historical ground truth.

finding: Cognate Transformer adapts aligned-sequence modeling; pretraining helps scarce-data settings.
formalization_use: Add an aligned neural proposer only after deterministic baselines.
caution: The reported limitations include metathesis, restricted families and weak small-data performance without pretraining.

finding: Jambu combines numerous South Asian etymological sources and tests reflex prediction.
formalization_use: Use source-aware imports and retain borrowing annotations.
caution: Large dictionary aggregates contain heterogeneous analyses, not a uniform sound-law theory.

finding: Trimming gap-heavy alignment sites increases the regularity of inferred correspondence patterns.
formalization_use: Save both original and trimmed alignments with an explicit transformation log.
caution: Improved regularity can partly result from discarding difficult evidence.

finding: The cognate-and-derivative shared task separates supervised and unsupervised settings.
formalization_use: Keep derivative relations distinct from cognacy in schemas and scores.
caution: A benchmark's combined label inventory may differ from comparative-method categories.

finding: Bidirectional semisupervised reconstruction benefits from deriving daughters from candidate ancestors.
formalization_use: Check reflex derivability as a necessary consistency condition.
caution: The authors explicitly lack evidence that model reasoning matches linguists; wrong ancestors can still predict daughters well.

finding: Cognate Transformer frames cognacy as supervised link prediction over alignments.
formalization_use: Preserve edge scores and make cluster construction a separate operation.
caution: Pairwise links do not automatically define a coherent historical equivalence relation.

finding: Reflex prediction reranks proposed protoforms and improves several benchmark results.
formalization_use: Use forward checking to filter or rerank proposals.
caution: A better forward score is not sufficient for unique inverse identification.

finding: Graphic and phonetic features distinguish cognates and borrowings in major Romance languages.
formalization_use: Audit borrowed, inherited and learned forms separately.
caution: The paper identifies oral versus written Latin and restricted language coverage as limitations.

finding: Selecting one synonym can change inferred tree topology; alternative encodings retain synonyms.
formalization_use: Preserve all attested synonyms and record the sampling policy.
caution: A single preferred lexeme per concept is an analytical decision, not neutral preprocessing.

finding: Sound-law induction is formulated as programming by examples with LLM-generated programs.
formalization_use: Use untrusted program synthesis with a restricted verified checker.
caution: Only 85 benchmark instances are reported; unrestricted Python programs can memorize examples and are not sound-law proofs.

finding: Ancestor-informed LLM tasks induce sound-change rules and transcribe Chinese dialect pronunciations.
formalization_use: Treat executable rule proposals as testable artifacts.
caution: Middle Chinese representations and modern dialect prediction do not directly validate Proto-Sino-Tibetan reconstruction.

finding: PIE Lexicon already uses ordered foma sound-law scripts to generate Indo-European forms.
formalization_use: Acknowledge direct finite-state reconstruction prior art and compare rule semantics.
caution: Its Glottal Fricative Theory and reported generation accuracy are project-specific claims; matching encoded data does not establish a unique PIE system.

finding: EtymDB-2.0 models fine-grained etymological relationships extracted from Wiktionary.
formalization_use: Import typed relations with source/version identifiers.
caution: Automatically extracted etymologies require source and philological validation.

finding: Sequence labeling predicts missing Romanian cognates and unattested Latin forms.
formalization_use: Test gap-filling without converting predictions into attestation records.
caution: An unattested predicted word remains a hypothesis.

finding: RoBoCoP supplies a Romance cognate/borrowing database and benchmark.
formalization_use: Use borrowing discrimination as a separate measurable task.
caution: Dictionary-based labels and language coverage constrain generalization.

finding: The comparative method includes correspondence classification, complementary distribution, phonetic interpretation and morphology; syntax poses distinct problems.
formalization_use: Formalize a sequence of justified judgments and distinguish structural correspondence from phonetic realization.
caution: Cognacy, typology and philological interpretation are substantive empirical inputs, not universally decidable facts.

finding: Computational elaborations split classical work into sequence comparison and language-classification problems within an iterative workflow.
formalization_use: Keep cognate proposals, alignments, correspondences and phylogeny as separate interfaces.
caution: No one fixed algorithm exhausts the comparative method.

finding: An ERC proposal motivates computer-assisted comparison and expert-computational cooperation.
formalization_use: Useful project-design context only.
caution: This is a proposal, not a research paper; excluded from the 100-work floor.

finding: Sound change includes contested mechanisms; phonologization, analogy and contact must be distinguished.
formalization_use: Give each mechanism a separate typed explanation and scope.
caution: A deterministic rewrite formalism describes outcomes without by itself explaining actuation.

finding: The chapter relates directional sound-change biases to production, perception and phonologization.
formalization_use: Treat phonetic naturalness as defeasible model preference.
caution: A common pathway is not a universal axiom that rules out all other histories.

finding: The classic Conspectus presents a taxonomy separating Chinese, Karen and Tibeto-Burman, with uncertain internal groupings.
formalization_use: Version historical taxonomies rather than importing their names as fixed types.
caution: Scanned PDF; only selected taxonomy pages were visually examined. Its taxonomy must not be silently treated as current consensus.

finding: The organic approach connects lexical variation and semantics while acknowledging uncertain higher subgrouping.
formalization_use: Preserve semantic variation and competing etymological groupings.
caution: Scanned monograph; selected introductory pages examined, not all lexical analyses.

finding: The critique distinguishes explanatory insight from symbolization and disputes overfilled protoforms and chronology.
formalization_use: Demand explanatory constraints and transparent alternatives in addition to formal derivations.
caution: This polemical exchange is evidence about methodological disagreement, not a verdict on every disputed etymology.

finding: Numeral reconstruction involves prefixes, uneven documentary evidence and revised subgroup assumptions.
formalization_use: Include numerals as structured morphology with explicit borrowing and source checks.
caution: Numerals are not automatically immune to borrowing or analogical replacement.

finding: A major systematic reference for Proto-Tibeto-Burman reconstruction and allofamic variation.
formalization_use: Required reference for future detailed model comparison; publisher description and scholarly reviews supply context here.
caution: Full PDF acquisition failed; the book is not counted or claimed as directly read.

finding: A substantial lower-level reconstruction separates Kuki-Chin, Central Chin, Northern Chin and Maraic sets.
formalization_use: Use a bounded subgroup pilot with taxonomic level stored for every protoform.
caution: A subgroup reconstruction is not a reconstruction of the whole Sino-Tibetan ancestor.

finding: Northern Chin reconstruction combines internal evidence with Old Burmese and Old Chinese comparisons.
formalization_use: Compare alternative evidence paths without merging their assumptions.
caution: External comparisons and broader two-vowel hypotheses require separate validation.

finding: The inventory reference documents language-specific transcription systems and phonetic interpretations.
formalization_use: Build explicit transcription adapters before comparing segment strings.
caution: The introductory count and the later website description differ; this study does not harmonize them into a false exact count.

finding: Secondary Tibetan -wa from syllable fusion is proposed to reconcile apparent counterexamples to monophthongization.
formalization_use: Test chronological layers and coalescence rather than exempting individual words.
caution: Observed -wa and reconstructed *-wa need not belong to the same historical stage.

finding: A review of Hill stresses contact, philological detail, analogy and unresolved correspondences.
formalization_use: Maintain multiple models and mark explicitly unexplained residues.
caution: The author praises methodological progress without endorsing a single completed Proto-Trans-Himalayan reconstruction.

finding: Tangut vowel alternations are analyzed through coalescence with a third-person patient suffix.
formalization_use: Model paradigms and morpheme boundaries before applying phonology.
caution: Similar surface alternations can reflect different historical morphological structures.

finding: A comparative morphology manuscript argues against treating tonal isolating typology as necessarily ancestral.
formalization_use: Keep synchronic typology separate from hypotheses about proto-morphology.
caution: Conference manuscript; reconstruction depends on better-established sound correspondences.

finding: Tangut verbal templates can resemble Rgyalrong through independent grammaticalization.
formalization_use: Represent inherited structure and parallel innovation as different hypotheses.
caution: Structural resemblance alone is insufficient to infer common inherited templates.

finding: Old Chinese tonal derivation is compared with diverse suffixes in morphologically rich Trans-Himalayan languages.
formalization_use: Allow several historical sources for one later tonal distinction.
caution: Chinese-language paper; first substantive page visually checked because text extraction damages characters.

finding: Several historical suffixes are proposed behind Old Chinese departing-tone derivation.
formalization_use: Keep homophonous suffixes and their functions distinct in reconstruction.
caution: The comparisons differ in strength; a single modern reflex need not imply one proto-morpheme.

finding: Khaling tone alternations partly follow coda loss and syllable reduction, with a remaining unexplained residue.
formalization_use: Represent tone as structured data and preserve residual failures.
caution: Do not manufacture an exceptionless account by deleting unexplained paradigm cells.

finding: Multiple diachronic pathways can yield aspirated fricatives, including Pumi evidence.
formalization_use: Use phonetic-feature models with multiple permitted histories.
caution: A feature analysis or typological pathway is not a unique inverse reconstruction.

finding: Historical sound glosses bear on Old Chinese morphology and syntax.
formalization_use: Attach dated gloss evidence to phonological analyses and syntactic claims.
caution: Later glosses are mediated observations with their own phonological systems.

finding: Japhug causative and abilitative derivations motivate grammaticalization hypotheses relevant to Sino-Tibetan prefixes.
formalization_use: Distinguish a shared-looking prefix from the history of its functions.
caution: Consensus about a prefix does not remove uncertainty about its origin and development.

finding: The *sr- comparison is reassessed with philological exclusions and an additional etymology.
formalization_use: A small explicit cluster correspondence makes a useful cross-branch pilot.
caution: Rejecting weak comparisons is as important as collecting supporting examples.

finding: Tibetan stem alternations are explained by hypothetical directional prefixes and ordered sound changes.
formalization_use: Represent internal reconstruction as a separate source of constraints and coindexed alternatives.
caution: Several prefix shapes remain underdetermined; comparison with Rgyalrong is not identity of historical systems.

finding: Rgyalrongic and Kiranti agreement are compared amid competing inheritance and innovation accounts.
formalization_use: Use paradigmatic evidence with explicit comparison units.
caution: Scanned article; the first-page argument was examined, not the full proof of each morphological comparison.

finding: Intransitive nasal prefixation is compared across Sino-Tibetan languages.
formalization_use: Require prefix segmentation and derivational-function evidence.
caution: Matching nasal segments without morphology does not establish one inherited prefix.

finding: The HPTB review asks for explicit, testable correspondences while recognizing useful rhyme reconstruction.
formalization_use: Make every correspondence retrievable and testable against counterexamples.
caution: A critical review does not substitute for direct inspection of the reviewed monograph; excluded from the conservative count.

finding: A 250-concept Old Chinese list retains 301 forms because some concepts have competing lexical candidates.
formalization_use: Preserve multiple lexemes and identify the Baxter-Sagart reconstruction version.
caution: Old Chinese reconstructed forms are analyses, even when the underlying written words are attested.

finding: A reply continues the disagreement over the testability of HPTB comparisons.
formalization_use: Archive disagreements at the level of particular claims and assumptions.
caution: A short methodological reply is excluded from the conservative 100-work count.

finding: The sketch distinguishes rhyme, script, Middle Chinese, loanword and dialect evidence for Old Chinese.
formalization_use: Keep observation types separate from a selected phonological reconstruction system.
caution: Baxter-Sagart is the sketch's adopted analysis, not a theory-independent transcription of Old Chinese speech.

finding: Competing accounts of *s- prefix effects differ on voicing, sonorants and derivational functions.
formalization_use: Build separately named rule sets and compare their predicted reflexes.
caution: A formally consistent system can still compete with a different consistent analysis.

finding: Initial laryngeal reflexes interact with syllabification and paradigmatic remodeling in Anatolian.
formalization_use: Use environment-specific and paradigm-aware laryngeal case studies.
caution: Scanned two-page spreads; selected examples do not establish a universal Hittite laryngeal rule.

finding: The work targets the conditioning of Sanskrit palatovelar depalatalization before r.
formalization_use: Reserve a named-law dossier for context and chronology tests.
caution: The article examines conditioning and apparent counterexamples; selected scanned pages were inspected, not every etymology.

finding: Anatolian evidence is used to compare competing nominal accent-ablaut reconstructions.
formalization_use: Represent accent, stem, suffix and ending as separate structured components.
caution: Do not encode one contested paradigm theory as the definition of PIE morphology.

finding: Anatolian and Tocharian evidence changes the analysis of thorn correspondences toward dental-velar clusters and metathesis.
formalization_use: Include a bounded metathesis extension after local substitution/deletion.
caution: Simple monotonic segment alignment cannot represent every proposed correspondence history.

finding: A length-based Anatolian stop interpretation motivates an Indo-Hittite reconstruction argument.
formalization_use: Separate observed spellings from phonetic interpretation and phylogenetic conclusions.
caution: The direction of typological reasoning is a scholarly hypothesis, not a Lean axiom.

finding: Old Hittite narrative aspect is compared with competing accounts of early PIE verbal categories.
formalization_use: Add morphological and semantic category reconstruction only with explicit textual evidence.
caution: An interpretive tense-aspect proposal requires more than sound-string derivations.

finding: The origin of Hittite hi-conjugation is debated through perfect and h2e-conjugation theories.
formalization_use: Treat rival morphological histories as alternative model packages.
caution: The common mi-conjugation comparison does not settle the contested hi-conjugation.

finding: A branch overview situates Anatolian languages, attestation and subgroup evidence.
formalization_use: Use it to define the scope and dates of an Anatolian pilot.
caution: Also contained in the downloaded Olander volume; this separate PDF is not counted as an additional work.

finding: The chapter links linguistic arguments for the Anatolian split with migration and ancient-DNA debates.
formalization_use: Keep linguistic derivations separate from archaeological and demographic arguments.
caution: Genetic populations and reconstructed speech communities are not interchangeable formal objects.

finding: A proposed pre-PIE final em-to-om law is evaluated against morphology, counterexamples and chronology.
formalization_use: Use a disputed law as a model-comparison test, preserving its exceptions and assumptions.
caution: This is a proposal to be tested, not settled background for all PIE derivations.

finding: IE-CoR distinguishes cognate relations, borrowing, morphological complexity and disagreements about protoforms.
formalization_use: Use source-rich cognate data without presuming a unique reconstructed string.
caution: The paper's abstract and body differ on total lexeme count; pin a dataset release and compute counts from files.

finding: Methodological and branch chapters distinguish shared innovation, retention, contact and limits of cladistics.
formalization_use: Anchor the PIE pilot in multiple authors and compare explicit chronologies.
caution: The full book is retained, but selected introduction, methodology and cladistics passages were studied, not all chapters.

finding: Lean's small trusted kernel checks explicit proofs while automation constructs them.
formalization_use: Place untrusted inference outside a proof-producing boundary.
caution: This describes an earlier Lean generation; implementation guidance must use the pinned Lean 4 release.

finding: Lean 4 integrates an extensible prover with a functional programming language.
formalization_use: Use executable definitions with proved correspondence to declarative semantics.
caution: Extensible elaboration and compiled execution are not automatically part of a trusted proof.

finding: Mathlib's shared abstractions and automation support a reusable formal library.
formalization_use: Reuse established finite sets, relations, graphs and automata where APIs fit.
caution: Historical architecture descriptions are not guarantees about current module names.

finding: Maintenance and linting address errors and usability beyond logical consistency.
formalization_use: Audit theorem statements, dependencies and documentation in CI.
caution: A kernel-accepted theorem can still formalize an unintended or vacuous statement.

finding: Typeclass design has tradeoffs involving bundled structures, inference and hierarchy complexity.
formalization_use: Pass empirical reconstructions as explicit parameters, not globally inferred instances.
caution: Competing historical assumptions should not be selected invisibly by typeclass search.

finding: Deprecation, linting and review tools help maintain a growing formal library.
formalization_use: Pin dependencies, budget migrations and keep a small stable public interface.
caution: Library growth and upstream changes impose ongoing engineering costs.

finding: Coq formalizations connect regular expressions, automata and decidable equivalence constructively.
formalization_use: Borrow proof architecture for verified finite-state compilation and counterexamples.
caution: A formalization of acceptors does not immediately supply two-tape transducers.

finding: Isabelle/HOL formalizes automata using hereditarily finite sets to manage state constructions.
formalization_use: Compare state-representation choices before committing to transducer infrastructure.
caution: The set-theoretic representation is a design alternative, not a directly importable Lean module.

finding: A verified MSO-on-words decision procedure is relevant to future logical transduction work.
formalization_use: Record as related work requiring direct acquisition before technical reliance.
caution: Download failed; not counted and not claimed as read.

finding: Sequential transducers and weighted determinization have specific applicability conditions.
formalization_use: State determinization hypotheses and distinguish functions from relations.
caution: Not every finite-state relation is a deterministic sequential function.

finding: Weighted automata algorithms depend on semiring structure and algorithm-specific conditions.
formalization_use: Start with Boolean or finite rational cases before infinite weighted-path sums.
caution: Composition, epsilon behavior and path multiplicity require explicit treatment.

finding: Weighted disambiguation has sufficient applicability conditions, including a weak twins property in the tropical case.
formalization_use: Require an applicability certificate before using a transformation as semantics-preserving.
caution: Termination and correctness do not hold without the stated restrictions.

finding: Sequence comparison requires precise alignment objectives; pairwise and multiple alignment differ computationally.
formalization_use: Formalize alignment validity first, and prove optimality only for a specified algorithm and scoring scheme.
caution: An optimal edit alignment can remain linguistically implausible; heuristics and analysis must stay distinct.

finding: Probabilistic models reconstruct Austronesian protoforms at large scale and compare with expert reconstructions.
formalization_use: Use model-based reconstruction as a serious baseline and source of candidates.
caution: Distance to an expert reconstruction measures agreement with that analysis, not direct access to ancient speech.

finding: A curated Sino-Tibetan cognate database supports dated phylogenetic inference.
formalization_use: Keep cognacy coding, topology and dating priors as separately versioned artifacts.
caution: A dated tree is not a completed phonological reconstruction of the root language.

finding: Ancestry constraints and coding choices affect Indo-European phylogenetic dating.
formalization_use: Include sensitivity analysis for sampled ancestors and lexical coding.
caution: This paper and Heggarty et al. use different assumptions; their conclusions must not be merged into a single proved homeland.

finding: Sampled-ancestor phylogenies support a proposed hybrid account of Indo-European origins.
formalization_use: Compare assumptions and data with ancestry-constrained alternatives.
caution: The downloaded author manuscript has a different title from the final article; geographic conclusions are model-dependent.

finding: Perfect-phylogeny-based cladistics uses explicit character coding to study Indo-European subgrouping.
formalization_use: Specify character validity and tree compatibility independently.
caution: The phylogenetic target is distinct from reconstructing word forms; decoding PDF glyph names was needed for the abstract.

finding: Phylogenetic networks extend trees with contact edges and fit an Indo-European character dataset.
formalization_use: Provide a future inheritance/contact graph layer with typed edges.
caution: An optimized contact network is conditional on character coding and optimization criteria.

finding: Simulation compares linguistic phylogenetic reconstruction methods under controlled scenarios.
formalization_use: Use synthetic histories with known latent structure as one evaluation track.
caution: Simulation accuracy depends on how realistic the generating process is.

finding: Answer set programming searches for a small number of contact edges on a phylogenetic tree.
formalization_use: Use solver-produced witnesses checked by an independent formal verifier.
caution: Solver output is not itself a Lean proof, and minimality needs additional evidence.

finding: A rates-across-sites model can make different divergence times observationally indistinguishable.
formalization_use: Treat identifiability as a theorem obligation rather than assuming more data settles every parameter.
caution: The result concerns a particular statistical model, not a universal impossibility theorem for linguistic dating.

finding: A proved reflective Coq tactic decides Kleene-algebra equations and returns counterexamples.
formalization_use: Emulate reflection and counterexample-producing checking for a restricted sound-rule language.
caution: A substantial algebraic formalization is needed; this is not an off-the-shelf Lean transducer checker.

finding: Restricted ordered phonological rewriting and two-level constraints admit finite-state treatments.
formalization_use: Define application semantics first, then prove compilation for a restricted fragment.
caution: Self-feeding and unrestricted rewriting need care; inverse relations can be ambiguous even when forward rules are deterministic.

finding: Input/output strictly local functions capture several local phonological processes and support learnability results.
formalization_use: Choose a small input-local fragment and make locality bounds explicit.
caution: Locality is a restriction to justify and test, not a claim that all historical changes fit one fragment.

finding: Two-level morphology is foundational background for relation-based phonological descriptions.
formalization_use: Track as an acquisition gap; Kaplan and Kay supply directly examined related formal analysis.
caution: The full original book was not downloaded or read here.

finding: CLDF provides interoperable tabular formats, reference vocabularies and validation.
formalization_use: Use CLDF as interchange while adding proof and provenance metadata.
caution: Syntactically valid CLDF does not ensure accurate cognacy or phonology.

finding: Lexibank standardizes heterogeneous wordlists and derives reusable features.
formalization_use: Pin dataset versions and preserve original versus normalized transcriptions.
caution: Standardization can lose distinctions unless transformation records remain available.

finding: Sound-correspondence-based phylogenies do not consistently beat cognate-based ones on the examined datasets.
formalization_use: Evaluate the value of each evidence type rather than presuming phonological input improves every tree.
caution: A more detailed representation can still perform worse under a particular inference model.

finding: Trimmed alignments and correspondence patterns support fast supervised reconstruction.
formalization_use: Adopt a transparent correspondence-based baseline before neural extensions.
caution: Training reconstructions are supplied labels, not independently verified ancestors.

finding: Fuzzy protoforms represent alternatives; the paper explicitly warns that position-wise alternatives take a Cartesian product.
formalization_use: Preserve joint candidate sets or coindexed constraints; the prototype exhibits spurious hybrid forms.
caution: Agreement across perturbed predictors is a stability measure, not a calibrated posterior probability.

finding: EDICTOR 3 integrates automated proposals with manual annotation and inspection.
formalization_use: Design exportable, editable dossiers around the verified core.
caution: An integrated workflow still needs a boundary between observed evidence and revised analyses.

finding: A methodological response argues that reconstructions in the two families have different evidential maturity.
formalization_use: Avoid assuming that a PIE-oriented method transfers unchanged to Trans-Himalayan data.
caution: Web PDF abstract examined; filesystem download denied, so not counted as a retained PDF.

finding: A proposed analysis links West Gyalrongic lenition with stress and compression in monosyllabicization.
formalization_use: Consider stress and intermediate stages in a later Sino-Tibetan rule extension.
caution: Only web-indexed introductory passages examined; download denied and metadata needs final publication verification.

finding: Morphophonological patterns can arise through analogy and become restricted to parts of paradigms.
formalization_use: Represent analogical replacement with its paradigm and model form, not as an arbitrary lexical exception.
caution: The same synchronic mapping can have distinct historical origins.

finding: Reanalysis alone can restate rather than explain syntactic change; analogy and grammaticalization provide alternative accounts.
formalization_use: Keep syntactic reconstruction a separately motivated extension with its own evidence.
caution: A verified tree transformation is not an explanation of historical directionality.

finding: The Reconstruction Engine already implements bidirectional comparison with contextual correspondences, syllable structure, semantic filtering and controlled imprecision.
formalization_use: Use this as direct prior art for a verified reconstruction checker, including its explicit residual class and distinction between correspondence and rule.
caution: A computer implementation is not a machine-checked correctness proof; user-supplied semantic and correspondence assumptions remain substantive.
